newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols take a breather after ECI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols take a breather after ECI.

text.p: Treasury bond options implied volatility levels cooled this morning following release of a key report on U.S. labor costs, but could veer up again heading into Friday's July payroll data, traders said.

Options traders had pumped up volatilities Monday in anticipation of this morning's second-quarter employment cost index. Just before the number was released at 0830 EDT, September bond volatility was quoted at 8.60 percent in both the 115-00 and 116-00 strikes, near the previous day's closing levels.
It subsequently was slashed to 8.15 percent in the 115-00s and 8.00 percent in the 116-00s by session end as the underlying futures continued their months-long uptrend.

ECI rose 0.8 percent, in line with analysts' expectations. The news propelled September futures to a fresh 1-1/2-year high. The contract added to gains in the afternoon, peaking at 115-31 before settling one tick below the high, up 1/2 point on the day.
Traders said volatility should uptick before Friday's July employment data, based on its behavior preceding past jobs reports.

Several other important pieces of economic data, including the advance second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product on Thursday and the national purchasing managers' July survey on Friday, also are coming out.
But one broker said the pre-employment volatility run-up may have become too predictable and hence less reliable, as a trend.
"We always expect it, but it doesn't always happen," he noted. Futures' steady grind higher is also acting as a drag on volatility by reducing uncertainty about price direction, he said.
"Volatility will inch higher Thursday through Friday, then drop to 7.75-7.60 (percent)," forecast a second floor broker.
Traders in both Treasuries and Eurodollars said brisk business in options throughout the day was the result of many market participants electing to hedge positions before the late-week reports.

In Eurodollar options, a U.S. banking firm's sale of 10,000 December 94.40/94.25 strangles was a standout, traders said. December Eurodollar volatility slipped 0.2 percentage point to 8.80 percent, while March was unchanged at 11.20 percent.
